issuer: Florida Department of Revenue, Office of Technical Assistance
title: Florida DOR Technical Assistance Advisement 88C1-003: Filing Requirement REIT Subsidiaries
subject: Filing Requirement REIT Subsidiaries
text:
Oct 20, 1988
Re: Technical Assistant Advisement TAA 88C1-003
Corporate Income Tax: Filing Requirement REIT Subsidiaries
s. 220.02(3), F.S.
Dear
Your letter of August 10, 1988 requested a technical
assistance advisement that a subsidiary of a real estate
investment trust (REIT) would not be treated as a separate
corporation for Florida corporate income tax purposes.
The pertinent facts presented in your letter are as
follows:
XXX (the "taxpayer") is a XXX business trust. The taxpayer
is the General Partner of XXX. ("XXX"), a Florida limited
partnership formed pursuant to that certain Agreement and
Certificate of Limited Partnership dated as of XXX 1982,
which was filed with the Department of State of the State
of Florida on XXX. XXX is a general partner in XXX (the
"XXX"), a Florida general partnership.
For federal income tax purposes, the taxpayer is a real
estate investment trust within the meaning of Section 856
of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended. The
taxpayer proposes to form a wholly owned subsidiary. The
subsidiary will be, for federal income tax purposes, a
"qualified REIT subsidiary" as such term is defined in s.
856(1), I.R.C. The taxpayer then proposes to contribute
its general partnership interest in XXX to its newly formed
subsidiary.
The treatment of REIT subsidiaries as provided in s.
856(i)(1), I.R.C. is:
(1) In general- For purposes of this title-
(a) a corporation which is a qualified REIT subsidiary

shall not be treated as a separate corporation, and
(b) all assets, liabilities, and items of income,
deduction, and credit of a qualified REIT subsidiary shall
be treated as assets, liabilities, and such items (as the
case may be) of the real estate investment trust.
As stated in s. 220.02(3), F.S.:
It is the intent of the Legislature that the income tax
imposed by this code utilize, to the greatest extent
possible, concepts of law which have been developed in
connection with the income tax laws of the United
States....
Therefore, a totally owned subsidiary of the taxpayer which
is treated as a qualified REIT subsidiary for federal tax
purposes will be treated in the same manner for Florida tax
purposes. The taxpayer would include the assets, liabilities,
and items of income, deductions, and credit of the qualified
REIT subsidiary on its Florida income tax return. The qualified
REIT subsidiary would not be required to file a separate return
for the Florida corporate income tax.
This response constitutes a technical assistance advisement
under s. 213.22, F.S., which is binding on the department only
under the facts and circumstances described in the request for
this advice as specified in s. 213.22, F.S. Our response is
predicated on those facts and the specific situation summarized
above. You are advised that subsequent statutory or
administrative rule changes or judicial interpretations of the
statutes or rules upon which this advice is based may subject
similar future transactions to a different treatment than
expressed in this response.
You are further advised that this response and your request
are public records under Chapter 119, F.S., which are subject to
disclosure to the public under the conditions of s. 213.22, F.S.
Your name, address, and any other details which might lead to
identification of the taxpayer must be deleted by the department
before disclosure. In an effort to protect confidential
information, we request you notify the undersigned in writing

within 15 days of any deletions you wish made to the request or
this response.
Sincerely,
Joan L. Davidson
Technical Assistant
